What is Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia?

A condition that results in enlarged prostate is referred to as Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH). The prostate gland contributes to the production of sperm in men, and it is fairly common for the prostate gland to grow larger as one gets older. An enlarged prostate is not something that should cause you a great deal of anxiety, but at the same time if you do nothing about it, it could trigger issues in a number of different ways.

Understanding enlargement of the Prostate Gland

Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia is influenced by a number of circumstances however, the precise cause of the condition is not completely understood. The chief contributors to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) in men are:

Hormonal Changes Associated with Aging

As men get older, their testosterone levels continue to fall, while their estrogen scale either remain the same or increase. An imbalance in hormones is thought to be the primary contributing factor in the growth of the prostate.

Dihydrotestosterone

A significant role for the formation and growth of your prostate gland is played by this testosterone derivative. The accumulation of increased levels of DHT of prostate, which can lead to enlargement, is more likely to occur in older men.

Lifestyle and Health

Excessive body weight can have an effect on hormone levels and contribute to the enlargement of the prostate for people who are obese. An insufficient amount of physical activity has been associated with an increased risk for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

Diabetes

Men with diabetes have an increased chance of developing benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Cardiovascular Health is connected to the health of the prostate, and there is a correlation between the two, according to specific research.

Symptoms of Enlargement in the Prostate Gland

Difficulty with Urine Flow

If you are suffering with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia, you would often experience difficulty in starting urination and finally emptying your bladder. This occurs because the enlarged prostate compresses the urethra and makes it harder for urine to flow completely out the bladder.

Weak Urine Flow

The most common symptom of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia is a noticeable decrease in the strength and volume of the urine stream. Because of an enlarged prostate the urethra narrows down in size and restricts urine flow, leading to a weak stream.

Urgency to Urinate

Patients with an enlarged prostate sometimes get a sudden, strong urge to urinate which can cause difficulty in delaying urination. This urgency can lead to situations were finding a restroom quickly becomes a priority.

Frequent Urination

An enlarged prostate gland can cause an increase in the need to urinate, especially during the night. This can significantly disrupt sleep patterns and daily activities.

Effects of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia on daily life

Disturbed Sleep

For patients with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia, it is possible for them to have a disturbed sleep routine because of frequent urination during the night. This insufficient amount of sleep can result in feelings of exhaustion, lower attention, and a general drop in productivity throughout the day.

Reduced Physical Activity

Men with suffering with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia can be demotivated from participating in activities when there is restricted access to restrooms due to the urgency and frequency of urine flow. This might result in a lifestyle that is defined as sedentary, which in turn can have an impact on one's general health and fitness.

Stress and Anxiety

The constant need to be near a restroom can cause significant stress and anxiety. Men with BPH symptoms may worry about embarrassing accidents or being in situations where they cannot easily access a restroom.

Professional Challenges

The enlargement of the prostate can cause the need for frequent bathroom breaks and can affect work performance and decrease productivity. Men may feel self-conscious about their condition, leading to decreased confidence in professional setting as well.

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is a procedure used to end a pregnancy using medication in the form of pills. This method is commonly used in the early stages of pregnancy usually up to 10 weeks of gestation. Medical Termination of Pregnancy is highly effective and considered one of the most safest and risk free procedure as it bears no threats to future pregnancies. 98 % percent of the time medical termination of pregnancy is extremely efficient and yields desired results.

Types of Abortion

1. Medical Abortion

MTP is the non surgical solution to abortion. Medical Termination of Pregnancy involves taking medication in the form of pills which blocks the effect of progesterone, the hormone needed for the pregnancy to continue. Mifepristone: This medication is taken first, usually at a healthcare provider's clinic. Mifepristone blocks the hormone progesterone, which is necessary for the pregnancy to continue. Misoprostol: This medication is taken 24 to 48 hours after the Mifepristone. Misoprostol causes the uterus to contract, leading to the expulsion of the pregnancy tissue. The medical abortion process typically takes place over few days, with the patient taking the medications and experiencing the abortion at home.

2. Surgical Abortion

Procedures such as the D and C technique which can be performed during the first trimester. During the procedure the doctor dilates the cervix with an instrument or medication, then scrapes the uterine lining with a spoon shaped instrument called a curette to remove existing tissue. D and E Abortion (Dilation and Evacuation Abortion), is another technique which is usually performed in the Second Trimester (mostly after 13 weeks of pregnancy ) The procedure is performed by dilating the cervix (the passage that connects the uterus and the vagina ) which is followed by the suction method.

What is Surgical Termination Of Pregnancy (STP)?

Surgical Termination of Pregnancy is a surgical procedure used to terminate a pregnancy. STP is performed in two ways namely, D and C (Dilation and Curettage) Abortion and Dilation and Evacuation Abortion (D&E Abortion). a. D and C (Dilation and Curettage) Abortion Dilation and Curettage Abortion is a surgical technique which is performed during the first trimester of pregnancy. During this procedure the doctor dilates the cervix with an instrument or medication, then scrapes the uterine lining with a curette (a spoon shaped instrument) to remove existing Fetal tissue. b. Dilation and Evacuation Abortion (D&E Abortion) : Dilation and Evacuation Abortion is a surgical procedure used to terminate pregnancy primarily during the second trimester. The procedure involves dilating the cervix and then using a suction instrument to remove the foetus and the placenta. However, when compared to D and C Abortion , Dilation and Evacuation Abortion (D and E Abortion) is a bit more complex to perform.

Aftercare and Recovery

Recovery phase is as important as choosing which type of procedure you are opting for. Whether you choose surgical or non surgical abortion, giving yourself time and making yourself comfortable during the entire process is crucial. Here are some key points to consider :

Bleeding and Cramping

  Bleeding is a common symptom post abortion and lasts on an average of about a week or so, depending on the individual and the chosen type of abortion. You may experience varying levels of bleeding and cramping, depending on the type of abortion and your individual response. If you are experiencing extreme bleeding for more than a day or two it is highly recommended to consult a health professional. Medical abortion: Moderate bleeding and cramping are typical, as the uterus contracts to expel the pregnancy tissue. Surgical abortion: Lighter bleeding and cramping are noticed, as the pregnancy tissue is removed directly. However, risk factors including in procedure complications are relatively higher. After your abortion, it is important to discuss birth control options with your healthcare provider to prevent an unintended pregnancy.

How soon after an abortion can you get pregnant?

A previous abortion does not affect the chances of a woman getting pregnant again nor does it affect her future pregnancies. Once the ovulation cycle starts which can be as early as 2 weeks, chances of the woman conceiving are back to normal.

How to remove retained products of conception after abortion?

In rare cases, some pregnancy tissue may remain in the uterus after an abortion. This is known as retained products of conception. If you experience prolonged bleeding or severe cramping, contact your healthcare provider, who may recommend a follow-up procedure to remove any of the remaining tissue.

Is Abortion Painful?

The experience of pain during an abortion varies from person to person and depends on the type of abortion procedure. Here’s what you can generally expect:

Medical Abortion:

  • Pain Level: Often described as similar to heavy menstrual cramps.
  • Duration: Pain typically starts within a few hours of taking the medication and can last for a few days.
  • Management: Over-the-counter pain relievers and prescribed medications can help manage discomfort.

Surgical Abortion:

  • Pain Level: Some people experience cramping during and after the procedure.
  • Duration: Pain is usually brief during the procedure and may continue for a few hours afterward.
  • Management: Local anesthesia, sedation, or general anesthesia are used to minimize pain during the procedure. Pain relievers can be used after the procedure.

Emotional Experience:

  • Emotional Pain: It's normal to have a range of emotions after an abortion, from relief to sadness. Support from friends, family, or a counselor can be helpful.

How to stop bleeding after abortion?

Understanding what to expect in terms of bleeding and recovery can help you manage the process more effectively. To manage bleeding after an abortion, follow these steps:
  1. Rest: Take it slow for a few days, allow your body to completely recover from the process.
  2. Pain Relief: Pain relievers like ibuprofen or paracetamol can be used to manage cramping and discomfort. Consult a health professional before proceeding further.
  3. Bleeding Management: Use sanitary pads rather than tampons until the bleeding stops. Avoid using tampons during the abortion process to prevent infection.

How Long After Abortion Do Symptoms of Pregnancy Go Away?

After an abortion, the symptoms of pregnancy will gradually diminish. Here's a general timeline of what to expect:

Immediate Changes:

  • Within a Few Days:
    • Nausea: Pregnancy-related nausea usually starts to improve within a few days after the abortion.
    • Breast Tenderness: Breast soreness and tenderness often begin to decrease within a few days to a week.

Varicocele, a condition marked by enlarged veins in the scrotum, can lead to complications such as infertility if not addressed. Traditionally, surgical options like laparoscopic varicocelectomy have been the standard treatment, but they come with significant risks and recovery times. Fortunately, advancements in medical technology have introduced non-surgical alternatives, such as varicocele embolization. This minimally invasive procedure allows for effective treatment without the need for major incisions, significantly reducing recovery time and minimizing complications. In this article, we will explore the nature of varicocele, traditional treatment methods, and the advantages of choosing embolization as a safer, more efficient option for managing this condition.

What is Varicocele?

A condition that results in a collection of enlarged veins in the Scrotum (the bag that holds a man's testicles) is known as Varicocele. Varicocele affects the veins that travel up towards the spermatic cord. The spermatic cord contains the tube that carries sperm from the testes to the penis, lymphatic vessels, and nerves. A Varicocele if left untreated, might affect the development of the testicles and may result in decreased sperm count leading to infertility.

Understanding A Varicocele

Definition of the Condition:

Varicocele is a swelling of the veins in the scrotum that usually happens when the valves in these veins fail, resulting in the blood to back up and pool. Although there is no specific reason that causes this condition, experts say that these might contribute to resulting in a Varicocele.

Hormonal Changes:

During puberty the testicles grow quickly and usually require more blood than normal. But if the valves in the scrotum don't function properly the veins won't be able to handle the extra flow of blood and causes it to pool up. This ultimately might be a key reason that can cause a Varicocele.

Defective Valves:

The valves in the veins are responsible for redirecting blood flow, so in case the valves in the veins of the scrotum don't function as usual then it causes the blood to accumulate in the same place causing swelling and Varicocele formation.

Blood Flow:

Generally, the left side of the testicular veins follow a different pathway than the right. Blood flow on the left side of the testicles is also greater than the right, which can result in a Varicocele.

Traditional Treatments for Varicocele

Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy:

Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy is an open surgery to treat Varicocele that involves making major incisions in the abdomen or groin. The procedure involves physically cutting the swollen veins and then closing the ends off. The incisions made in the abdomen or even the groin is closed with stitches or staples.

Risks associated with Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy:

Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy is an open surgery which means the risks associated with it are relatively high. As a matter of fact, in any open surgery the chances of failures or even complications are on the upper side. But, for a surgery such as a Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy which is performed in a very sensitive organ like the Scrotum, risks involved shoot up furthermore. Some of them are listed below
  • Excessive Bleeding
  • Blood Clots
  • Severe infection
  • Fluid formation around the testicles (Hydrocele)
  • Scarring
  • Decrease in Sperm Count

Varicocele treatment without surgery

With centuries worth of knowledge combined with advancement in technology and medicine, today there are multiple non-surgical solutions to various ailments and diseases that the common man is unaware of. For a condition such as a Varicocele, Embolization is perhaps the most well-known non-surgical treatment option that is available. In this procedure, an interventional radiologist uses a coil or special agents to block or embolize the affected veins. This can then improve the overall symptoms.

What is Varicocele Embolization?

Varicocele Embolization is a procedure that involves redirecting blood away from an enlarged vein in the scrotum. A radiologist uses a coil or special agents to block or embolize the vein which reduces the swelling and allows the blood to flow without causing it to pool up. Varicocele Embolization is also a minimally invasive technique with no major cuts or incisions involved.

Advantages of Varicocele Embolization Over Traditional Surgery

Compared to other surgical procedures available for Varicocele, Varicocele Embolization is a minimally invasive technique which means that it involves no major incisions or cuts to be performed.

An open surgery involves the doctor to make major cuts or incisions on the patient which takes a lot of time to heal and recover. Since this procedure is a minimally invasive technique which does not involve major incisions or even cuts, the patient usually recovers from the procedure in no time.

What happens in the Process of Varicocele Embolization?

Pre-procedure preparation

First, you’ll be given medicine to make you feel comfortable, relaxed and sleepy. The area where the procedure is to be performed will be cleansed to avoid any sort of infection. A small incision is made through the inner part of the upper thigh and a Catheter is sent through. A Catheter is a thin, flexible tube used to carry micro particles or special agents. One of the major veins is accessed through this small incision and with the help of x-rays an interventional radiologist will move the tube to the correct area in your scrotum and then a small coil or a special liquid will be inserted into the affected vein. This is called a blocking agent. This redirects the blood flow into other nearby veins and helps the blood to exit the scrotum normally. After the procedure the catheter will be removed, and a bandage will be placed on the area of entry on your thigh.

This technique is a Day Care Procedure, in other words it does not require the patient to get admitted for days and allows them to get discharged as soon as the treatment is over. Also, since the procedure is minimally invasive, the patient can get back to resuming normal activities in a couple of days. As mentioned, the recovery time span for patients undergoing this procedure is very less when compared to other surgical alternatives.

The most important aspect of this procedure is that it provides the patient the ability to recover quickly. It is a day care procedure which means that the patient can go home the same day. The procedure does not involve any scarring or suture and all it does is redirects the blood flow in the veins of the scrotum and thereby reduces swelling, removes blood clot and provides permanent relief from other symptoms of Varicocele. For these reasons it is considered one of the most advanced and safest procedures when compared to its surgical counterparts.

Since varicoceles frequently arise naturally, they cannot be prevented. Early intervention, however, can avoid problems and reduce symptoms

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act of 1971 of India outlines the specific grounds under which abortion is permitted in the country. For pregnancies between 20 and 24 weeks, abortion is permitted as an exception, but only under specific categories, such as cases of sexual assault, rape, or fetal abnormalities. These cases require the approval of two registered medical practitioners. After 24 weeks, the law mandates the formation of a medical board in approved facilities to determine if termination is allowed based on substantial fetal abnormality. However, the Supreme Court has granted permission for abortions beyond this period in certain exceptional cases, such as those involving minors or severe health risks to the pregnant woman.

Is Abortion Legal in India for Unmarried Women?

Yes, abortion is legal in India for unmarried women, but the grounds are slightly different compared to married women. For unmarried women, abortion is permitted under the same grounds as for married women, such as:
  • The continuance of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to her physical or mental health.
  • There is a substantial risk that if the child were born, it would suffer from such physical or mental abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped.
  • The pregnancy is caused by rape.
  • The pregnancy is caused by failure of any contraceptive device or method used by a married woman or her partner.
However, the MTP Act does not explicitly mention unmarried women as a separate category. In practice, unmarried women may face additional barriers or scrutiny when seeking abortion services, as societal stigma and moral judgments can play a role. Ensuring access to abortion services for unmarried women is crucial for upholding their reproductive rights.

The MTP Act strictly regulates who can perform abortions and where they can be conducted. Evolution of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act

  • 1971: The original MTP Act allowed abortion up to 20 weeks of pregnancy under certain conditions.
  • 2021: The Act was amended by the to increase the upper gestational limit for abortion from 20 to 24 weeks in certain cases, such as fetal abnormalities or pregnancies resulting from sexual assault.

What is it?

Having a condition that results in a collection of enlarged veins in the scrotum (the bag that holds a man’s testicles) is known as Varicocele. Varicocele affects the veins that travel up towards the spermatic cord. The spermatic cord contains the tube that carries sperm from the testes to the penis, lymphatic vessels, and nerves. A varicocele might affect the development of the testicles and may result in decreased sperm count leading to infertility.

Symptoms of Varicocele Akshay – crop the top part of the pic saying “varicocele symptoms complications and treatment” A varicocele often occurs on the left side of the scrotum and predominantly does not produce any signs or symptoms. However, possible indications might include : Pain:     A stiff feeling down below which gets relieved when lying down. Size:     A difference in the size of testicles might also be the result of this condition. Often the affected testicle may be smaller than the other one. Infertility:   A varicocele might affect sperm count and reduce fertility but at the same time cannot be the only cause. Causes of Varicocele?

There is no specific reason that causes this condition and doctors aren’t sure as to why it occurs. However, it usually takes place in teens because of their quick growth during puberty.  During development, the testicles need more blood than normal as they grow significantly in this stage and thereby any blockage might cause this condition.

Treatment : Open Surgery : A typical surgery can help treat varicoceles. This is done under general anesthesia and will need several days/weeks for recovery. Varicocele Embolization: Varicocele Embolization is a procedure that involves redirecting blood away from an enlarged vein in the scrotum. A radiologist uses a coil or special agents to block or embolize the vein. This can then improve the overall symptoms What happens during the procedure? The procedure usually takes a few hours and in general, you might expect the following :
  • You’ll be given medicine to make you feel comfortable, relaxed and sleepy first.
  • Then you’ll receive a shot of numbing medicine into an area on the inner part of your upper thigh, this will prevent you from feeling much during the procedure.
  • The health care provider will then clean the area, they will then put a needle into your inner thigh to access a major vein and they’ll insert the catheter tube into this vein.
  • With the help of x-rays your provider will move the tube to the correct area in your scrotum and then a small coil or a special liquid will be inserted into the affected vein. This is called a blocking agent . This redirects the blood flow into other nearby veins and helps the blood to exit the scrotum normally
  • After the procedure the catheter will be removed and a bandage will be placed on the area of entry on your thigh.
As far as recovery is concerned it is a lot quicker than a typical surgery given a couple of days of rest. Take away : If you have symptoms of varicocele talk to your doctor and find out what treatment suits you best at the same time don’t panic since this is completely treatable provided the right method is used.

Infertility is defined as being unable to get pregnant after a year of unprotected sex when the woman is within her reproductive age. There are various reasons why a woman experiences infertility. Apart from abnormal ovulation, sperm count and motility, one of the common reasons for infertility is the blockage in fallopian tube(s).   • One-third of the couples with infertility have an issue with both partners.
Why is infertility on the rise?
  • One of the main reasons why women experience infertility is the choice of a higher age to get pregnant. With an increase in age, the quality of eggs produced decreases
  • The natural aging process also increases the chances of miscarriage.
  • The quality of sperm decreases with men aged over 40.
Lifestyle Factors that play an important role in fertility :
  • Smoking tobacco can damage sperm quality and affect the reproductive hormones of both men and women.
  • Alcohol too has an alarming effect on the reproductive system and is strictly prohibited during pregnancy.
  • High levels of stress also leads to irregular menstrual cycles.

Fallopian tube Recanalization is a procedure that does not involve an open surgery or laproscopic surgery.   • Placing a speculum into the vagina and passing a small tube also known as a catheter through the cervix into the uterus.
  • Examining the uterine cavity using an Xray camera.
  • Determining the area of blockage in the tube
  • Finally clearing the blockage using the catheter.
Over 90 % of the time the fallopian tube blockages can be removed which helps in increasing the chance of getting pregnant naturally and avoiding other fertility treatments such as IUI or IVF. Ramesh Krishnan and Sumitha Karthik are the Co-Founders of Medagg Healthcare, Tamil Nadu’s largest hospital discovery platform are on their way to transform patient experience in hospitals. We are honoured to have two stalwarts from the industry in our midst, and begin by probing into the core idea driving the journey. Below are excerpts from the exchange.

THE BIG IDEA

EVOLUTION CURVE

This is what led us to the idea of formalizing this advisory in the form of Medagg.”

SOLVING FOR X

All driven leaders have a burning target they want to crack. The x in the proverbial equation. What is your X? “Medagg hopes to become the largest hospital discovery platform. We have started off with Tamil Nadu and have already aggregated more than 1000 hospitals in the state. THE DIFFERENTIATOR

What sets them apart from others in the market? “As opposed to some of the recent surgery consolidation platforms which limit the number of affiliated hospitals per city,, Medagg works out of a much larger affiliation base of hospitals. content:
Piles, are also called Haemorrhoids, are enlarged blood vessels that you can get inside or around your anus, which is the opening of the bottom. It’s normal to have blood vessels in the anus, as they play an essential role in incontinence. But piles can develop if these blood vessels become enlarged. It is a lump that is found in that particular area. The size of the piles might vary from person to person. Piles can be internal or external too. Internal piles are customarily located above the opening of the anus, and they are the more common type. External piles occur on the outside edge of the anus.

Types Of Piles
There are by far two types of hemorrhoids which are Internal and External. Internal Piles Internal piles are so far inside the rectum that you can’t usually see or feel them. However, they don’t generally hurt because of a few pain-sensing nerves there. They are not visible to the naked eyes.

External Piles External piles get formed in the anal region and create discomfort. When an external haemorrhoid protrudes through the anus, it can be seen and felt. Sometimes blood clots can form within the mass that slips down; it can be harrowing.
Symptoms Of Piles
Internal piles rarely cause pain, and they typically can’t be felt unless they collapse. Many people with internal haemorrhoids don’t know they have them because they don’t have symptoms. If a person has internal piles symptoms, they might see blood on toilet paper, stool, or toilet bowl. These are signs of rectal bleeding.
Signs Of External Piles Include:
  • Itchy anus
  • Hard lumps near the anus that feel sore
  • Pain or ache in the anus, especially while sitting
  • Rectal bleeding

Causes Of Piles
Straining puts pressure on veins in the anus or rectum, causing haemorrhoids. Any straining that increases pressure on the belly or lower extremities can cause anal and rectal veins to become swollen and inflamed. Haemorrhoids may develop due to:
  • Pelvic pressure from weight gain, especially during pregnancy.
  • Pushing hard to have a bowel movement due to constipation.
  • Straining to lift heavy objects or weightlifting.

Treatment For Piles
Non-Surgical Medication Several therapeutic options are available to make symptoms more manageable for an individual with piles. Over-The-Counter (OTC) These are available over-the-counter or online. Medications include painkillers, ointments, creams, and pads to help soothe redness and swelling around the anus. OTC remedies do not cure piles but can relieve the symptoms. Please do not use them for more than seven days in a row, as they can cause further irritation of the area and thinness of the skin. Also, do not use two or more medications simultaneously unless advised by a medical professional. Corticosteroids These can reduce inflammation and pain. Laxatives The doctor may prescribe laxatives if a person with piles suffers from constipation. These can help the person pass stools more efficiently and reduce pressure on the lower colon.
Minimally Invasive Procedures
For continuous bleeding or painful haemorrhoids, the doctor might recommend one of the minimally invasive procedures available. These treatments can be done in your doctor’s office or different outpatient settings and don’t usually require anaesthesia. Rubber Band Ligation The doctor places one or two tiny rubber bands around the internal haemorrhoid to cut off its circulation. The haemorrhoid shrinks and falls off within a week. Haemorrhoid banding can be uncomfortable and cause bleeding, which is rarely severe. Injection (Sclerotherapy) The specialist injects a chemical solution into the haemorrhoid tissue to shrink it. While the injection causes little or no pain, it might be less effective than rubber band ligation. Coagulation (Infrared, Laser Or Bipolar) Coagulation techniques use laser or infrared light or heat. They cause slight, bleeding internal haemorrhoids to harden and wither. Warm Bath Warm baths can help soothe irritation from haemorrhoids. Using a sitz bath, a small plastic tub that fits over a toilet seat can immerse the affected area. Trying a warm or sitz bath for 20 minutes after each bowel movement and Adding Epsom salt to the tub can provide further relief. Cold Compress Applying ice packs or cold compresses to the anus can relieve swelling for 15 minutes at a time. For large, painful haemorrhoids, cold compresses can be highly effective. Make sure to wrap ice inside a cloth or paper towel. Never apply something frozen directly to your skin since this can harm or damage the skin. Do Not Scratch Scratching damages the skin and worsens the irritation and itching. Apply Coconut Oil Coconut oil is a natural moisturiser that may also help with haemorrhoid symptoms. In addition, applying coconut oil may reduce the irritation and swelling, and it may also help reduce the urge to scratch. Try Squat

Try a squat position. For example, put a short bench under your feet when you go to the bathroom. Raising your knees as you sit on the toilet changes the position of your inner workings and could make bowel movements easier.
Conclusion

Understanding the common anal and rectal conditions of piles is essential for effective management, including piles treatment and haemorrhoids prevention. By being aware of the causes, symptoms, treatment options, and prevention tips, individuals can take proactive steps towards maintaining anal and rectal health. Remember, if you have any concerns or questions, it is always advisable to consult a healthcare professional for further guidance and support. Take control of your well-being and prioritise your digestive health.
People Also Ask

1. What Is The Leading Cause Of Piles? Piles occur due to chronic constipation, chronic diarrhoea, lifting heavy weights, pregnancy, or straining when passing a stool. 2. How Do I Know If I Have Piles?

A person with piles may experience the feeling that the bowels are still full after passing a stool. Bright red blood is visible after a bowel movement. The area around the anus is itchy, red, and sore. Pain occurs during the passing of a stool. 3. How Do Piles Go Away? There is no set duration for haemorrhoids. Small haemorrhoids may clear up without any treatment within a few days. Large, external haemorrhoids may take longer to heal and cause significant pain and discomfort. If haemorrhoids have not resolved within a few days, it is best to see a doctor for treatment. 4. What Foods Cause Piles? Foods with little fibre can cause constipation (and therefore haemorrhoids) worse, so it’s best to limit how much you eat of them.
  • White bread
  • Milk, cheese, and other dairies
  • Meat
  • Processed foods such as frozen meals and fast food
Watch the amount of salt you consume because It can lead to your body hanging on to water, putting more pressure on your blood vessels. That includes the veins in your bottom that cause haemorrhoids.

content:
Goal to become the Airbnb in healthcare is what made Medagg possible says Ramesh Krishnan, Board Member, Sahyadri Hospitals and Dr. Rela Institute and Medical centre and Managing Partner at MEDAGG VENTURES LLP

    “The buying behaviour in which people are buying healthcare services is constantly changing. This is one of the reasons I say that the industry is nowhere near steady state,” says Ramesh Krishnan, Board Member, Sahyadri Hospitals and Dr. Rela Institute and Medical centre and Managing Partner at MEDAGG VENTURES LLP.       Data aggregation is the process of combining information from multiple databases to produce cohesive, shareable information. When it comes to healthcare data, the benefits of sharing are plentiful as from pharmaceutical and biotech companies to care providers, the healthcare sector demands evidence-based decision-making now more than ever. Ramesh Krishnan, Board Member, Sahyadri Hospitals, which is a large West India chain of Hospitals. He is also a board member of Dr. Rela Institute and Medical centre, Managing Partner at MEDAGG VENTURES LLP, and the Operating Partner at Ever stone Capital. Medaag Ventures LLP is a team of experts who specialize in operations and management, strategic consulting, and transaction advisory services in the healthcare industry. Medagg Venture’s goal to become the Airbnb in healthcare Ramesh throws light on the subject, “Medical Aggregation was the theme that Medagg as a firm was founded on. We work on aggregation at various levels. The eventual goal would be to become Airbnb in healthcare by aggregating secondary neighborhood hospitals. To this end, we have already put together a pipeline of hospitals and are in the process of raising funds. In the meantime, we also apply the principles of medical aggregations in a few more areas as well. For example, we run channel partnerships for a few innovative startups in the healthcare space which help aggregate specific healthcare services across multiple hospitals from a central command centre. ER, ICU, e-pharmacy, central procurement, etc are a few to name. We also partner with a few innovative service providers in commoditizing some common but underprovided treatments like varicose veins by bringing about scale. This we believe could become a huge game-changer in the daycare space,” he says.   Bringing value addition to hospital operations Ramesh explains, “Medagg also runs strategic advisory services and Transaction advisory services which again focus on bringing value addition to hospital operations through aggregation concepts. I feel that the secondary hospital market is so fragmented that consolidation is inevitable for that segment of the market even to survive. This is the reason we focus so heavily on the aggregation as a theme. It is ironic that at a time when the country needs more treatment beds, one segment of the already installed beds (secondary hospitals) are struggling for survival since they are sub-scale and are not able to handle costs. This actually makes it an ideal case for consolidation,” he says A journey of more than 25 years in the Pharmaceutical and Healthcare industry
Ramesh talks about his journey, “Healthcare has always been a very fulfilling profession for me. In fact, moving from Pharma to Healthcare delivery has been even more gratifying because you are directly connected to patients. There is so much more that could and must be done in this industry which is still not near equilibrium when it behaves like a steady-state. After 25 years in large corporate, I felt that I could contribute more in the affordable healthcare segment by aggregating services if I go out on my own and that is how Medagg was born,” he says.
Healthcare nowhere near steady-state Ramesh shares his thoughts on the future outcomes we should watch out for in terms of Healthcare, “The buying behavior in which people are buying healthcare services is constantly changing. This is one of the reasons I say that the industry is nowhere near steady-state. The penetration of insurance is still below 50% in the country. Insurance still does not cover daycare and outpatient treatments. This is primarily because of the fact that primary and secondary healthcare segments are still very fragmented and run like mom-and-pop stores with no large corporate chains having established presence as yet. These are inevitable changes that are bound to come about in the coming few years. These will help consolidate and organize the primary and secondary healthcare segments. A number of startups with interesting products and services are springing up of late, which will all aid to bring about this consolidation. The number of people buying healthcare online is also constantly on the increase. An OYO or Airbnb kind of consolidation in the healthcare space is bound to happen as this would become a basic line of survival for many struggling secondary hospitals. The hospital wards are continuing to be extended out to peoples’ homes with homecare constantly on the increase. This is not only increasing the availability of beds in hospitals in a country that is below global averages in bed provision but also reducing the level of hospital-acquired infections. The government has made its intentions clear that it wants to provide healthcare to its entire population of 1.3 billion people. But it has also made it clear that it will remain as a payor and will not get into provision. The provision is left to the private sector to fulfill. In a social industry like healthcare where the government takes the role of a payor and leaves the provision to the private players, price regulations become a norm. We have started seeing this already and this will only increase. This will call for more innovation to be rolled out in this space. So with this entire churn happening in the industry, we can expect a very exciting, challenging, and innovative decade ahead for Indian healthcare,” he says.   The medical fraternity more confident in handling the sick due to COVID Ramesh presents his views, “It is true that COVID is not going away in any hurry. But it is also true that our medical fraternity has become a lot more confident in handling the sick. To be honest, I am keener to see an established line of treatment for the disease than even the vaccine. So the fact that our doctors are a lot more confident in treating patients is actually good news. While COVID has indeed established a new normal in the way we go about doing our day-to-day activities, I also see a huge opportunity for innovation, especially within the healthcare space. We will of course have to take the obvious precautions before we get out of this pandemic fully. We cannot drop our guard as yet. However, I do see things coming back quite quickly albeit with caution,” he says.
